messages:
ashley: Quick heads-up — I'm assembling a tiny quickstart for the Optimize Toolkit that focuses on sensible defaults for batching + KV cache + a 4-bit quant profile. Goal: one page, runnable examples in Python + JS, and a short table of tradeoffs. Draft PR is up.
kevin: Can you drop the PR link? I can help with the JS snippet.
ashley: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4823 (WIP).
ashley: TODOs I see: (1) add runnable Node + Python snippets, (2) include a tiny config YAML for quant profile, (3) add a note on latency vs cost, (4) run the snippets through CI/sample harness.
leah: I can take the Python example. Which runtime call do we want to show? `optimize.run_batch()` or the lower-level `inference.request()`? Prefer showing the high-level Optimize API so users get the recipe.
maria: For SDK v2 the idiom is `client.optimize.batch()` in both py/js examples. Keep the Python code to ~8 lines. Include `kv_prefetch: true` and `batch_window_ms: 20` as the recommended starting point.
kevin: I'll draft the Node snippet. idea:

```js
// Node example (short)
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient();
await client.optimize.batch({
  model: 'llama-70b-q4',
  batch_window_ms: 20,
  kv_prefetch: true,
  prompts: ['summarize: ...']
});
```

kevin: Is `llama-70b-q4` the correct sample model name? I want it to reflect an open/quantized variant.
ashley: Yes, that's fine — but in the doc we should recommend `llama-70b-4bit` as the friendly label and note the catalog alias. Add a footnote about pinning model version for repeatability.
leah: Python snippet (first pass):

```py
# Python quickstart
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.optimize.batch(
    model='llama-70b-4bit',
    batch_window_ms=20,
    kv_prefetch=True,
    prompts=['Write a micro-summary of this text...']
)
print(resp[0].text)
```

leah: I'll submit a small patch with that.
maria: Quant profiles — we should ship two small examples inline: `fast` (prioritizes latency, less aggressive quant) and `economy` (more aggressive quant + caching). Something like:

```
profiles:
  fast:
    quant_bits: 8
    kv_prefetch: false
    batch_window_ms: 10
  economy:
    quant_bits: 4
    kv_prefetch: true
    batch_window_ms: 30
```

maria: We also need a short note about expected perf: "fast" ~ lower tokenization latency, higher cost; "economy" ~ lower cost, might add ~10-40ms tail depending on cache hit rate.
kevin: Can someone run the snippets against the sample harness so CI doesn't flake? I can run Node locally if someone pushes the sample inputs.
ashley: docs-bot: preview? :) 
docs-bot: deploy-preview available at https://deploy-preview-4823--redwood-docs.netlify.app/optimize/quickstart (auto)
leah: Thanks — I'll push the Python PR patch shortly and tag reviewers.
ashley: Reviewers: @maria for quant text, @kevin for JS example, @eng-runtime for any runtime caveats. Also ask eng-ml for a quick sanity check on the perf numbers.
maria: Quick comment — add a one-line callout: "If you rely on strict ordering or low p99, prefer smaller batch_window_ms and enable KV cache selectively."
kevin: LGTM. I'll check the Node example against the SDK tomorrow and report any API mismatch.
ashley: Great. Plan: land examples + profile table in PR4823, then follow with a short sample notebook (separate PR) with perf scripts. Anyone object?
leah: No objections. :+1:
maria: All good from docs side.
kevin: :rocket:
ashley: Thanks everyone — I'll keep the thread updated when CI preview shows real numbers.
